safety_verdicts.content: Patient has also been vomiting, with no blood in the vomit.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes vomiting but does not include the Gold detail of no blood in vomit.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the negative finding of no blood in vomit removes an important red-flag screen for upper GI bleeding, which can influence triage urgency and differential diagnosis. While the patient’s overall picture is still consistent with gastroenteritis, loss of this detail can lead to less reliable clinical decision-making or unnecessary escalation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions only one child vomiting with no diarrhea; it does not include Gold's statement that the wife is also unwell with vomiting.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the wife is also vomiting reduces the accuracy of the sick-contact history, which helps distinguish contagious gastroenteritis from foodborne/toxin-related or other causes and may affect public health/work advice. This is unlikely to directly change immediate management in an otherwise stable case but can impair assessment and counseling.
